add.issue.comment.md: Picking this up as zai/milo. Plan: small bash helper identity/workspace-id.sh — canonicalize checkout via git rev-parse --show-toplevel + pwd -P (symlink aliases collapse), derive repo-group id from the resolved --git-common-dir, workspace id as hestia-<label>-<hash12> (sha256 of canonical path, first 12 hex; label = sanitized bounded basename). Optional --state-dir records/verifies the full canonical path so mismatch or collision fails before reuse. Encoding/truncation documented in identity/README.md and covered by tests/workspace-id.test.sh built on throwaway temp repos (same-basename paths, worktree vs main, branch switch, symlink alias, forged record, moved checkout).
add.issue.comment.author: DHVZX3S2Z2CWHY35XK5ZWY12R9

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: Implemented in PR #2 (commit d66a3d0 on main, rebase-merged). identity/workspace-id.sh canonicalizes a checkout (git show-toplevel + pwd -P, symlink aliases collapse incl. macOS /var vs /private/var) and prints canonical/repo-group/workspace. Workspace id hestia-<label>-<hash12> from the canonical path; repo-group from the resolved --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir (needs git >= 2.31; host has 2.55) so main checkout and linked worktrees share the group with distinct workspace ids. Label: lowercased ASCII [a-z0-9-], runs collapsed, bounded to 24 chars, fallback "repo"; hash: first 12 hex of sha256 over the UTF-8 path; total <= 44 chars matching Compose project-name rules (verified against docs.docker.com). Optional --state-dir records the full canonical path + ids; later runs fail before reuse on path mismatch ("refusing to reuse") or id collision, never rewriting old state.

Verified 2026-09-09 on macOS 25.6.0 arm64, git 2.55.0: tests/workspace-id.test.sh passed 16/16 (form/bounds, sanitization + truncation, same-basename distinct paths, worktree vs main, branch-switch stability, symlink alias, non-git/missing-path failures, record write/reuse, moved-checkout rejection with record intact, forged-record collision). CodeRabbit passed; its only flag was advisory docstring-coverage heuristics for bash. JP73P2D and 24GJSHY can consume this helper.

add.issue.comment.md: Picking this up as zai/milo (deps 61Q7E8F + SKSJTMN both Done). Plan: extend the canonical root Dockerfile with a second stage (FROM the base stage) that COPYs the fixture mise.toml and runs mise install during the explicit build, keeping one build path (base target unchanged; tools land in an image layer, not persistent state). Verify: build the stage, run the fixture source build/tests inside the container with recorded versions; prove no startup installation with --network none runs; show a missing/undeclared tool fails clearly; document that only the build-context mise.toml is trusted deliberately (mounted repos stay untrusted until JP73P2D defines runtime trust).
add.issue.comment.author: DHVZX3S2Z2CWHY35XK5ZWY12R9

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: Implemented in PR #4 (commit 06d0dbf on main, rebase-merged). fixture-tools stage in the canonical Dockerfile (base target unchanged, one build path): the fixture mise.toml becomes the dev user global toolchain config — root-owned so the runtime user cannot modify it — installed by mise install during the explicit build only; the fixture go build/test runs as the build-time toolchain check and its source is removed in the same layer.

Key finding on deliberate trust: mise 2026.9.4 normal mode AUTO-TRUSTS a project active config — observed directly: a never-trusted mounted mise.toml task executed unchallenged. The stage therefore sets MISE_PARANOID=1; verified cycle: untrusted mounted config blocked with a clear error, runs after mise trust, re-blocked after a content edit (content-bound), runs after re-trust; the image global config needs no prompt. mise docs note paranoid also disables trust sharing across git worktrees — relevant to JP73P2D.

Other verification 2026-09-09, macOS 25.6.0 arm64, Docker server 29.5.2: fixture-tools build 17s, image sha256:3031b761d8a9... 227971940 bytes; docker run --network none reports go1.27.1 with zero downloads (no startup install); mise exec -- node fails with a clear error; base target rebuilds to the identical base image ID. Evidence in docs/evidence.md, including the pitfall that a macOS /tmp bind mount is silently empty in Docker Desktop (use shared paths for mount proofs). CodeRabbit passed, no findings.
